headline_en: Conflict with employer led to the arrest of VENUS-1 — diplomats intervened
text_en: Conflict with employer led to the arrest of VENUS-1 — diplomats intervened The fishing vessel VENUS-1 with 13 Russian citizens on board has been arrested in Namibia. This was reported by the Russian embassy in the country. According to the diplomatic mission, the cause was a labour dispute between the crew and the owner of the vessel — the private company Hodago fishing. The conflict arose at the beginning of 2026 over two months of unpaid wages. As specified, after the intervention of the International Transport Workers' Federation, the vessel was arrested and is moored at the berth in the port of Walvis Bay together with the crew. Russian diplomats are working with the Namibian authorities to resolve the situation. The embassy maintains contact with the captain and the sailors, and is also organising the supply of fuel and food to the vessel. The diplomatic mission stressed that there is no threat to the life and health of the Russians. The Namibian side, according to the embassy, is not preventing their return home. The crew made the decision to stay and seek a settlement of the conflict on its own. Work to resolve the situation is continuing. The diplomats stated their intention to seek respect for the rights of Russian citizens and a speedy end to the dispute. Read also: Russian sailors are living on an arrested vessel in Africa.

headline_en: Dozens of journalists left the Pentagon en masse over Hegseth's new rules
text_en: Dozens of journalists left the Pentagon en masse over Hegseth's new rules On October 15, American journalists who covered the activities of the US Department of Defense left the Pentagon after they were stripped of their accreditation for refusing to agree to tightened access rules. This is reported by the Associated Press and The Washington Post.According to AP, about 40–50 reporters left the building simultaneously, handing in their passes and carrying personal belongings out of their workplaces.Read alsoCensorship in a new way: how Donald Trump is rewriting the rules of the game for journalistsIt is noted that at least 20 news organizations did not agree to the Pentagon's new rules on journalists' access. Only the TV channel One America News Network signed the agreement.Former Voice of America journalist Ostap Yarysh explained the day before that the Pentagon's new rules prohibit journalists from obtaining any information, even unclassified, from their sources without official approval from the ministry, restrict movement around the building to only a few corridors, require constantly wearing bright red badges in addition to the regular ones, and "much more".The new policy was introduced by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.BackgroundOn September 19, 2025, the Pentagon introduced new rules for journalists, which provided for a ban on collecting or publishing any unauthorized information, even if it is not classified. For violating these requirements, journalists could be stripped of their accreditation. headline_en: TBMM Fisheries and Aquatic Products Research Commission Completed Its Work
text_en: TBMM Fisheries and Aquatic Products Research Commission Completed Its Work Chairman of the TBMM Fisheries and Aquatic Products Research Commission İsmail Emrah Karayel, stating that the commission had completed its work, said: 'Whatever needs to be done to clear the way for the sector, especially fishing and aquaculture, we as the commission will put forward that will. We want to set out the basic issues clearly and solve them quickly.'The commission convened under the chairmanship of AK Party Istanbul Deputy İsmail Emrah Karayel.Describing the activities carried out during the 4-month working period of the parliamentary research commission established to investigate the problems experienced in the fisheries and aquatic products sector and to determine the measures that need to be taken, Karayel recalled that they first invited sector stakeholders and representatives of professional organizations to Parliament and listened to their problems and demands, and then made field visits.Explaining that they carried out examinations regarding fishing activities in the Aegean, the Mediterranean, the Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara as well as in inland waters, Karayel said: 'As the commission, we have done about 190 hours of work to date. In our visits and examinations, 2 thousand pages of minutes were taken and we travelled 11 thousand kilometres. Thus we have completed the 4-month working period of our commission.'Conveying the issues most requested from the commission, Karayel the working conditions of aquatic products engineers, increasing the bank financing granted to producers in the sector, holding a campaign to increase fish consumption, increasing Turkish salmon production farms, a zoning regulation regarding fishing shelters, an ÖTV regulation regarding the fuel used by fishermen, and the fishing season

headline_en: Graffiti and protests. A European capital has joined the wave of anti-tourism
text_en: Graffiti and protests. A European capital has joined the wave of anti-tourism The capital of Greece has joined the wave of protests against excessive tourism that has been spreading across Europe since last year. Now the walls of buildings in Athens are covered with graffiti with anti-tourist inscriptions. Residents are increasingly complaining about the housing crisis, RBC-Ukraine reports, citing greekcitytimes.com. Greece, which is one of the most popular countries in Europe among tourists, is now suffering from excessive tourism. Athens greets guests with graffiti on the walls bearing threatening inscriptions. Last month, residents of the historic city took to the streets to express their dissatisfaction with the influx of tourists. Protesters complain not only about overcrowding due to the large number of tourists, but also about the "displacement" of local residents from their homes. Because of the housing crisis, aggravated by tourism, city dwellers are forced to move. On the buildings one can see inscriptions: "Tourists, go home! The Greek state kills", "Tourism kills the city", "No tourists – no hipsters", "Burn Airbnb". The anti-tourist actions in Athens reflect similar movements across Europe, from Menorca to the Canary Islands, where residents demand measures to reduce the negative consequences of mass tourism. As a reminder, we wrote that a popular European city has declared war on tourists. The centre of Malaga is plastered with stickers with anti-tourism slogans.
